safeHtml:
| jctdir1 = '''Southbound''' | jctdir2 = '''Northbound''' | junctions = }}

'''Route 10''' is one of the Routes in Los Sengas. It runs between Rover and Torrent, connecting with Glacier, Ingress, Egress, Yowah and Cometsilk in the process.

Districts Served

  • Rover
  • Upper Rover
  • Peacean Island
  • Glacier
  • Ingress Flatland
  • Spike End
  • Ingress
  • Circle Pit
  • Ingress Sea
  • Comrel Island
  • Egress
  • Outcave
  • River Rendezvous
  • Yowah
  • Icelute Island
  • Flamelute Island
  • Yowah North
  • Diamond Sand
  • Calmé
  • Cometsilk
  • Silk Pond
  • Gentle Island
  • Torrent
  • Intus Orient

History

The initial route of Route 10 extends from the two north-south oriented roads at Prosand Station as a northeastern bypass of Los Sengas. This route enables drivers to travel between sub-urban areas of Los Sengas Continent without passing through its center. As this route radiated from Prosand, a large detour is made within Prosand at the time of this Route's construction, causing the route length to exceed 43 km.

When Route 10 began services, there were only 4 exits, namely at Circle Pit, Prosand, Stardust Road and Spinstone Plane, and was also the first Route to feature a non-expressway section. Along the route, the Junction between Warsaw Road and Marisa Road featured traffic lights, and due to sparse development, traffic was also very low. Hence, buses also avoided this route. However, before 2020, this route was the only external access to and from Intus Orient Village, causing vehicles to and from Intus Orient to pass through Cometsilk central very frequently and bottlenecks were formed.

However, as development at Los Sengas east began, Prosand, Egress, Comrel Island, Peacean Island and Clouds saw significant development, and Route 10 became a main artery at the east of Los Sengas, seeing an increasing traffic flow by the day. Vehicles to and from Intus Orient could now make use of Route 2 as well. Under these circumstances, the detour at Prosand became a problem for drivers who wanted to travel between Rover, Ingress, Egress and Torrent as it increased the travel time significantly without any alternatives provided. Moreover, regardless of the route taken, passing through Prosand was mandatory for drivers, further increasing traffic loads at the Warsaw Road, Ning Yat Road, Marisa Road Junction.

As a result, the re-routing works for Route 10 was proposed in 2021, with the new section extending to the south from east Diamond Sand, forming a junction with Route 2 at the east of Calmé, before joining the original Route 10 between Gentle Island and Waterbelt Garden. The works began in April 2022 and has since been completed. Currently, passengers between Clouds and Egress no longer had to pass through Prosand, and the section at Marisa Road is no longer a part of '''Route 10''', significantly shortening the length of '''Route 10''' from 43 km to 32 km.

Chronological Order

  • January 13 2018: '''Route 10''' began construction.
  • January 14 2018: Section between Intus Orient and Prosand completed construction.
  • January 15 2018: Section between Prosand and Flamelute Island completed construction.
  • January 16 2018: Section between Flamelute Island and Glacier completed construction.
  • January 17 2018: Section between Glacier and Upper Rover completed construction. '''Route 10''' completed construction.
  • April 5 2022: '''Route 10''' rerouting works began construction.
  • January 26 2025: This route becomes connected with Route 3.

Fun Facts

  • At the time of its completion, this route was 43.07 km long, and is still the longest Route in Los Sengas to date.
  • This route is the quickest route to complete construction, with the route completing construction just 4 days after construction began.
  • The Sheung Yuen Bridge along this route is the longest suspension bridge in Los Sengas at 4000 m long.
  • This Route wass the first Route in Los Sengas to feature a non-expressway section, with Marisa Road featuring Traffic Lights. However, after the latest re-route, this is no longer the case.
  • All sections of this Route have their independent road names, a rare instance among Routes in Los Sengas.

'''Route 2''' is one of the initially planned Routes in Los Sengas. It is designed to provide transport services for Los Sengas Continent, and had extended to Cometsilk and Clouds on April 2018. Currently, it is 19.131 km long.

History

  • April 2015: Plans for this route are in place.
  • May 8 2015: Metropolis JCT, Po Fong Exit completed construction.
  • June-July 2015: Metro Spring Exit, Katadelphia Section completed construction.
  • August-September 2015: Threeler Exit completed construction.
  • October 2015: Sava Section completed construction.
  • November 2015: Flask West, Flask East Exits completed construction.
  • December 30 2015: Grass Crack Exit completed construction.
  • December 31 2015: Sava-Yowah section began services.
  • 2016: Bonyal JCT, Southend Exit completed construction.
  • April 2018: Weaving Plate Exit, Twelve of June Bridge completed construction.
  • March 2022: Route 2 extended to Clouds.
  • January 23 2023: High Approach Road South Exit completed construction.

Fun Facts

  • Despite being the second route to be planned, Route 2 is the first route in Los Sengas to be constructed.
  • The Metropolis JCT has been subject to multiple re-constructions.
  • Bonyal and Southend Exits are only constructed later on.
  • The west end of this Route connects directly to Route 3.
  • Exit 4 is re-constructed due to construction.
  • San Annis Station of shares structure with this route.
  • Parts of shares structure with this route (Between and )
  • Flask East exit is the first loop exit in Los Sengas.

Development Trivia

Original Plans of Route

Before the official construction of this route, the suggested proposals of this route are as follows:https://www.facebook.com/groups/projn/permalink/1729503393946074/</ref>

  1. North Route: This route branches off from Route 2 near Jayler Road, and passes through Ponsand Island, Ponrest Island and Belt Island before approaching Peckern near Gull Woods, with no exits set up along the route. This route is represented by the red line at the picture below, and later became the route for at West Metropolis Archipelago.
  2. Central Route: This route branches off from Route 4 near Lean Forest Island, and passes under Middle Island, Info Island and Bulldoze Island before landing near Peckern Forest, with exits added upon request of island owners. This route is represented by the yellow line at the picture below. Ultimately, this route was chosen after a few modifications were made to it. Instaed of landing at Lean Forest Island, the current '''Route 5''' involves passing through Hatace Island and Seat River, with the Peckern end being located at Milead Pond.
  3. South Route: This route also branches off from Route 4 near Miner Bay Depot. However, instead of going to Peckern, it goes to Twenty-Second Continent after passing through Shony Island and Tenbal Island using tunnels and bridges, before passing through Airship Island to reach Peckern. It is represented by the orange color at the picture below, and later became the route for Route 7.
  4. Car Ferry Proposal: This route involves using a train that carries cars, and reaches Peckern Continent using a newly built railway tunnel. While detailed plans for this proposal never surface, it is implied that travels in a similar route to what this proposal could have used.

Fun Facts

  • Exit 9 of this Route provides connections with Cities Transit Route 5 Station.

This route originally passes through Python, but as Kallen Road has alread replaced the section of Route 7 that runs along Python, this route has now detoured to the north and merges with the original plans of Route 8 and heads for Peckern Continent.

Original Plans of Route

There were many proposals of the route for Route 7, and they are listed as follows;

  • This route involves Route 7 turning to the east and setting up an exit at Airship Island before landing at Blu Trove Bay of the Peckern Continent after passing through the Comp Ward JCT.
  • Airship Island, Wood Wound Route:
  • This route involves Route 7 going to Airship Island using a bridge and connecting to Wood Wound Road at Peckern Continent afte rpassing through the Comp Ward JCT. However, the setting up of the exit at Airship Island would be dependent on developmental needs.
  • Branch Proposal:
  • This proposal skips Airship Island and goes directly to Peckern Continent, connecting with Peckern Viaduct and setting up exits at Milead Pond and Wood Wound in the process. While this proposal was ultimately adopted, Route 7 was instead connected directly to Peckern Coast Bridge Road and intersects with Peckern East Coast Road to save construction costs. However, this proposal was highly dependent on transportation connections around Milead POnd, and connection works are done around Milead Pond during construction works.

Afterwards, Pekcern developers began reconstructing the above proposals and caused Route 7 to land on Airship Island on June 2022, before connecting to Dufol along the mountains of the south coast for preliminary works of Dufol Transport. The Peckern Section of Route 7 is subsequently named "Greater Development Predicament Expressway".

Subsequent Development

Suggestions have been made to extend Route 7 to Xofa in order to enhance connectivity. This proposal from Twenty-Second Continent was approved by developers from Peckern, but it was delayed to July 2022 due to difficulties at the Peckern section.

History

  • September 15 2016: Route 7 began construction.
  • September 16 2016: Nick Fin Bridge completed construction.
  • September 18 2016: Diamond Pool Bridge completed construction.
  • January 3 2020: Diamond Pool North JCT completed construction.
  • January 9 2020: Zerda Hill Exit, Java Beach Exit completed construction.
  • January 11 2020: Comp Ward Exit completed construction.
  • January 12 2020: Milead Pond JCT, Wood Wound Exit completed construction.
  • February 2 2020: Halozy Exit completed construction.
  • June 20 2021: Xofa Bypass completed construction.
  • April 2 2022: Halozy Exit completed reconstruction.
  • July 21 2022: Peckern Section completed reconstruction.

Future Development

When Route 7 began planning development at Nagasora, a branch at Darey Terrace was built to Nagasora to reduce traffic flow at Kallen Road. However, this plan was replaced by a new road (Serendipity Drive) connecting Routes 7 and 8, and Route 8 is instead used for Trunk Road Traffic to and from Nagasora.
